prerequisites: A noun names a person, place or thing; a pronoun can stand in for a noun phrase.
Distinguish the main action/state from words describing a noun.
explanation: The head is the central noun or pronoun of the subject phrase, not necessarily the noun nearest the verb. First find the main finite verb, then ask who or what that verb is about. Bracket prepositional phrases, relative clauses and participial modifiers. A coordinated subject can have two heads. In an inverted sentence the subject may follow the verb.

worked.action: In The basket of apples is heavy, the main verb is is and the subject phrase is The basket of apples.
worked.justification: The sentence says that the basket is heavy; apples describes what it contains.

worked.action: Bracket [of apples]; basket remains as the subject head.
worked.justification: The noun inside a prepositional modifier is not automatically the main subject.

worked.action: In Each of the players has a badge, Each is the pronoun head.
worked.justification: The of-phrase specifies the set; the sentence considers each member separately.

worked.action: In The student who carries the books is here, student heads the main subject; who heads only the relative clause.
worked.justification: Separate the main verb is from the embedded verb carries.

worked.action: In The bags left near the door belong to Meera, bags is the head and left near the door is a participial modifier.
worked.justification: A descriptive participle is not the main finite verb belong.

worked.action: In The author and the translator are present, author and translator are coordinated heads.
worked.justification: And combines two subject heads. Along with does not perform the same grammatical job.

worked.action: In Beside the gate stands a guard, the main verb stands precedes its subject a guard.
worked.justification: Do not select the first noun merely because it appears earlier. The guard stands; the gate gives the location.

worked.action: In One of the envelopes is open and Neither of the answers is complete, One and Neither are subject pronouns.
worked.justification: The nearby plural nouns belong to modifying of-phrases.

hint: Find the main finite verb. Bracket modifiers, then identify the noun/pronoun the main clause is about.
shortcut: Bracket of/to/near phrases before checking the head; restore them afterward to verify the meaning.
limitation: Do not erase words mechanically: distinguish true coordination, relative-clause subjects, passive agents and inversion.
